VoiceStudio

Open-source voice cloning, voice design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription & audiobook creation in 646 languages.

Website · Download · Get started · Docs · Discord · 简体中文 · 日本語

![A tour of the Electron app: voice cloning, voice design, dubbing, and model management](docs/media/electron/voicestudio.gif) ## Your voice. Your workflow. | Create | Produce | Connect | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Clone a voice or design your own | Dub videos with timed speech | Local API & MCP for agents | | Dictate with a floating widget | Stories, audiobooks & batch jobs | Reusable recipes & watch folders | Start with **VoiceStudio** (default, powered by k2-fsa/OmniVoice), or choose another engine. [Features & engine catalog](docs/feature-catalog.md). Local workflows run on your hardware. Remote services are optional; usage analytics requires consent.
Explore the workspaces · Clone, dub, design & models
Voice cloningVideo dubbing
Voice designLocal models
OmniVoice GGUF source builds can optionally use Vulkan on Windows and Linux; see the [native engine guide](docs/engines/omnivoice-gguf.md#optional-vulkan-acceleration) for build requirements, CPU fallback, and device overrides. ## Get started ### One-command install (macOS / Linux) ```sh # Latest Electron release curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh # A specific published Electron release (replace X.Y.Z) curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh -s -- --version X.Y.Z # Build current main and install the desktop app curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh -s -- --main # Uninstall the app, keeping your data curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh -s -- --uninstall ``` On Windows, run `irm https://voicestudio.sh/install | iex` in PowerShell. If `voicestudio.sh/install` is unreachable or returns 404, run the same script straight from the repository, or clone it and run `scripts/install.sh`: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/main/scripts/install.sh | sh ``` Release downloads require curl and a SHA-256 tool. `--main` requires Git, Node.js 22+, Bun, Rust/Cargo, and platform build tools; see [installer prerequisites and behavior](docs/install/script.md). The installer preserves your settings, projects, and models. Older versions must contain Electron packages; it never falls back to archived Tauri builds. Or download from [Releases](https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/releases/latest) (macOS `.dmg`, Windows `.exe`, Linux `.AppImage` or `.deb`, Android `.apk`, iPhone `.ipa`; or `sudo snap install voicestudio` on Linux) and follow your platform guide: **[macOS](docs/install/macos.md) · [Windows](docs/install/windows.md) · [Linux](docs/install/linux.md) · [Docker](docs/install/docker.md) · [Android and iPhone](docs/mobile.md#install)** | Hardware | Support | |---|---| | NVIDIA GPU (Windows / Linux) | CUDA acceleration | | AMD Radeon / supported Ryzen AI (Windows) | CPU by default; [opt-in Windows ROCm setup](docs/install/windows-rocm.md) for AMD's Windows 11 hardware matrix. Setup distinguishes package repair from host failures; install the VC++ runtime manually first. Optional engines have separate limits; Vulkan engines retain their own runtime. | | Apple Silicon (M1–M5) | Metal (MPS) acceleration | | AMD GPU | Opt-in native CosyVoice GGUF can use Vulkan when the community runtime is built with Vulkan; verified on RX 6700 XT ([setup](docs/engines/cosyvoice-gguf.md)) | | No dedicated GPU (Intel/AMD integrated graphics, older PCs) | Fully usable on the CPU, slower; setup installs the small CPU build of PyTorch (about 5 GB free disk) | | Windows on ARM (Snapdragon X etc.) | **Experimental**, validation pending: native ARM64 app, x64 Python backend under emulation, CPU only | | Intel Mac | App UI only; connect to a remote backend ([why](docs/install/macos.md)) | | Android phones (Android 10+) | **Preview**: models run on the phone, offline once downloaded ([install](docs/mobile.md#install)) | | iPhone and iPad (iOS 17+) | **Preview**: models run on the device; sideload the IPA with your Apple ID ([install](docs/mobile.md#install)) | Open **Voice cloning**, choose a voice or add a clean reference recording, enter your text, and generate. Install the required model when prompted. Hardware needs vary by engine; see [performance](docs/performance.md). ### Install with prompt Paste into your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …): ```text Install the VoiceStudio Electron app on this device and verify it works, following https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/blob/main/docs/install/agent.md ``` The [agent guide](docs/install/agent.md) covers hardware detection, reusing existing data, asking before model downloads, and a test generation. Agents that support skills can also run `npx skills add debpalash/VoiceStudio`.
Run the Electron preview from source ```bash git clone https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio.git cd VoiceStudio bun install bun run setup:api # prepare Python dependencies before starting Electron bun run dev ``` See [Electron setup](electron/README.md) for prerequisites and backend configuration. Use `bun run smoke-test` to build and launch an isolated packaged Electron app. Add `-- --install` for the networked managed-runtime installation check.
> **Electron is the only desktop app and web UI.** Version 0.5.3 was the final Tauri release. Existing Tauri users must [install Electron separately](docs/electron-migration.md). The retired Tauri shell and legacy UI entry points have been removed. ## Documentation | Need | Start here | |---|---| | Setup help | [Troubleshooting](docs/install/troubleshooting.md) · [Model downloads](docs/downloading-models.md) | | Models & audio quality | [Engine guides](docs/engines/README.md) · [whisper.cpp ASR](docs/engines/whisper-cpp.md) · [Benchmarks](docs/benchmarks.md) | | Integrations | [Local API](docs/speech-platform.md) · [MCP](docs/mcp.md) · [Examples](examples/README.md) | | Phone apps (preview, run offline) | [iOS and Android](docs/mobile.md) | | Development | [Contributing](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) ([CLA signing guidance](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#contribution-licensing) for your first PR) · [Electron](electron/README.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) | Agent skills: `npx skills add debpalash/VoiceStudio` — choose **voicestudio** for audio workflows or **voicestudio-maintainer** for repository maintenance. ## Team ### Core team

details.readme:
# Hallmark **A design skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode that refuses to look AI-generated.** [usehallmark.com](https://www.usehallmark.com)  ·  forty-eight themes  ·  custom on request  ·  redesign and audit by name Made by Together AI.

Hallmark holds a hard floor and then gets out of the way. It deals three themes from a catalog of forty-eight materials, builds the page around what the visitor came to do, and lints the result in a real browser against the tells that read as machine-made: the eyebrow above every heading, tracked-capital labels, one coloured word in a headline, a page of empty frames or nothing but photographs, a hero that misses its screen, an email sign-up at the end of every page, a form that says thanks without sending anything. A fresh-context reviewer gets the last word. The gates come in tiers. The **Floor** never ships (contrast, focus, reduced motion, invented facts, a broken phone layout). **Reflex** gates are the defaults a model falls into; a build with a reason may overrule one on the record. **Finish** checks are craft detail that never blocks a ship. ## New in v2 - **Forty-eight themes.** Each is a material (paper, type, colour, surfaces, its own components and texture) with a picture of a finished page, and the build lays out its own page in it. - **Built from the job.** A booking page books, a shop sells, a newsletter subscribes: the action sits where the category puts it, and the page ends on it. - **Custom.** Ask for a custom page and Hallmark designs from your prompt alone, under the same rules and checks. - **Your real product.** Point it at a URL, a dev server or an app and it captures the screenshots itself. - **Real photographs.** 755 openly licensed photos, picked per subject and credited on the page. - **Redesign and audit.** `/hallmark redesign ` rebuilds a page and keeps its content and wiring; `/hallmark audit ` only reports. ## Themes
Dusk
Closewise, bank reconciliation		 Cobalt
Relay, a webhook API		 Studio
Field Office, an identity studio		 Atelier
Maison Orla, a fragrance atelier		 Ribbon
Lull, a sleep sounds app
Furrow
Fieldbook, farm records		 Dose
Tandem, a family medication app		 Hum
Sprout, a reading game for kids		 Terminal
burrow, a dotfiles CLI		 Hedgerow
Five Mile Gin, a distillery
Ten of the forty-eight. A theme is a material, not a plan: it never says what a page contains or in what order, so two prompts in one theme make two different pages. Each is one file of at most 8 KB in [`references/themes/`](skills/hallmark/references/themes/) with a picture beside it; a build reads exactly one. See them all at [usehallmark.com](https://www.usehallmark.com). ## Custom Say **custom** and Hallmark drops the themes: no plan, no components, no palette recipe, only the floor, the gates and a short direction in [`direction.md`](skills/hallmark/references/direction.md) to find one idea that only this client has and let it run the page. ## How a build runs 1. Pre-flight reads the project (fonts, palette, framework, a locked `design.md`) and asks once for the material: photos, screenshots, real numbers. Nothing is invented. 2. `scripts/theme.mjs deal` offers three themes that fit the prompt and clear the log; `draw` deals the page's anatomy from its job. 3. The hero is built alone, rendered and reviewed cold before the rest of the page exists. 4. `scripts/sloplint.mjs --render` checks the page at eight widths, then a subagent reviews it with fresh eyes. Each page is self-contained HTML and CSS, stamped in its first CSS comment with the decisions it took. ## Redesign Hallmark never starts on a design that already exists unless you name it: ``` /hallmark redesign ./src/app /hallmark audit ./index.html ``` A full redesign keeps the content and the wiring and changes the system and the layout; say *keep the layout* for a restyle or *polish* for only the tells. `sloplint --before` records every link, field, handler and heading first, `sloplint --kept` fails the redesign if one went missing, and the handoff is a side-by-side before and after. ## Install ``` npx skills add nutlope/hallmark -g ``` `-g` installs for every project; leave it off to install into the current one. Needs Node 18 or later. The browser checks (`sloplint --render`, screenshots) also need `npm i -g puppeteer-core` and Chrome; without them the static checks still run. | Harness | Lands in | Invoke | | --- | --- | --- | | Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills/hallmark` | `/hallmark ` or describe a new build | | Codex CLI | `~/.agents/skills/hallmark` | `$hallmark ` or describe a new build | | Cursor | finds the copies above | `/hallmark ` or describe a new build | | OpenCode | finds the copies above | `/hallmark ` or describe a new build | - **One harness only:** `npx skills add nutlope/hallmark -g --agent claude-code` (or `codex`, `opencode`, `cursor`, `github-copilot`). - **As a Claude Code plugin:** `/plugin marketplace add nutlope/hallmark`, then `/plugin install hallmark@hallmark` (invoked as `/hallmark:hallmark`). - **From a clone:** `node skills/hallmark/scripts/install.mjs` validates every theme and reference before it copies; `install-hook.mjs` adds an edit-time Floor check to Claude Code. - **Lint any page:** `node skills/hallmark/scripts/sloplint.mjs --render`. - **If it does not fire on its own,** name it: *use hallmark to build ...*. ## Licence MIT. Use it, fork it, ship it. The photo library (`skills/hallmark/scripts/photos.json`) lists photographs hosted on Wikimedia Commons and holds no image files. Each keeps its own licence (CC0, public domain, CC BY or CC BY-SA), and Hallmark credits every one it uses on the page. It does not use stock sites (Unsplash, Pexels, Pixabay), whose terms bar AI tools from picking their images.

details.readme:
# Impeccable

Design guidance for AI coding agents. 1 skill, 24 commands, live browser iteration, and 62 deterministic detector rules for AI-generated frontend design.

> **Quick start:** From your project root, run `npx impeccable install`, then run `/impeccable init` inside your AI coding tool. Full docs: [impeccable.style](https://impeccable.style).

## Why Impeccable?

Anthropic's [frontend-design](https://github.com/anthropics/skills/tree/main/skills/frontend-design) was the first widely-used design skill for Claude. Impeccable started from there.

Every model trained on the same SaaS templates. Skip the guidance and you get the same handful of tells on every project: Inter for everything, purple-to-blue gradients, cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, the rounded-square icon tile above every heading.

Impeccable adds:
- **One setup flow.** `/impeccable init` records durable product truth in `PRODUCT.md`, so later commands know the audience, purpose, operating context, constraints, voice, and evidence without confusing those facts with surface-level visual direction.
- **24 commands.** A shared design vocabulary with your AI: `polish`, `audit`, `critique`, `distill`, `animate`, `bolder`, `quieter`, and more.
- **62 deterministic detector rules** plus LLM-only critique checks. The CLI and browser extension run the deterministic rules with no LLM and no API key.

## What's Included

### The Skill: impeccable

The skill installs as one command:

```bash
/impeccable <command> <target>
```

Start every new project with:

```bash
/impeccable init
```

`init` inspects the project, asks only for material gaps in durable product truth, and writes `PRODUCT.md`. Visitor mode and visual direction are chosen later for each surface; incumbent or newly built visual systems are recorded separately in `DESIGN.md`.

### 24 Commands

All commands are accessed through `/impeccable`:

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `/impeccable craft` | Full shape-then-build flow with visual iteration |
| `/impeccable init` | One-time setup: gather durable product context, write PRODUCT.md, configure live mode when applicable, recommend next steps |
| `/impeccable document` | Generate root DESIGN.md from existing project code |
| `/impeccable extract` | Pull reusable components and tokens into the design system |
| `/impeccable shape` | Plan UX/UI before writing code |
| `/impeccable critique` | UX design review: hierarchy, clarity, emotional resonance |
| `/impeccable audit` | Run technical quality checks (a11y, performance, responsive) |
| `/impeccable polish` | Final pass, design system alignment, and shipping readiness |
| `/impeccable bolder` | Amplify boring designs |
| `/impeccable quieter` | Tone down overly bold designs |
| `/impeccable distill` | Strip to essence |
| `/impeccable harden` | Error handling, i18n, text overflow, edge cases |
| `/impeccable onboard` | First-run flows, empty states, activation paths |
| `/impeccable animate` | Add purposeful motion |
| `/impeccable colorize` | Introduce strategic color |
| `/impeccable typeset` | Fix font choices, hierarchy, sizing |
| `/impeccable layout` | Fix layout, spacing, visual rhythm |
| `/impeccable delight` | Add moments of joy |
| `/impeccable overdrive` | Add technically extraordinary effects |
| `/impeccable clarify` | Improve unclear UX copy |
| `/impeccable adapt` | Adapt for different devices |
| `/impeccable optimize` | Performance improvements |
| `/impeccable live` | Visual variant mode: iterate on elements in the browser |
| `/impeccable generate` | Generate variants of a named element in the live browser, no manual picking |

Use `/impeccable pin <command>` to create standalone shortcuts (e.g., `pin audit` creates `/audit`).

#### Usage Examples

```
/impeccable audit blog           # Audit blog hub + post pages
/impeccable critique landing     # UX design review
/impeccable polish settings      # Final pass before shipping
/impeccable harden checkout      # Add error handling + edge cases
```

Or use `/impeccable` directly with a description:
```
/impeccable redo this hero section
```

### Anti-Patterns

The skill includes explicit guidance on what to avoid:

- Don't use overused fonts (Arial, Inter, system defaults)
- Don't use gray text on colored backgrounds
- Don't use pure black/gray (always tint)
- Don't wrap everything in cards or nest cards inside cards
- Don't use bounce/elastic easing (feels dated)

## See It In Action

Visit [the Neo Mirai case study](https://impeccable.style/cases/neo-mirai) to see a before/after case study of a real project transformed with Impeccable commands.

## Installation

The skill needs no runtime of its own. Every skill copy ships a small launcher (`scripts/impeccable`, plus `impeccable.cmd` for Windows) that runs the Impeccable engine, a self-contained binary that either sits next to the launcher or is downloaded once on first run into `~/.impeccable/bin/`. Node is only involved if you use the `npx impeccable` installer, which is a shim around the same binary; the manual and Git options below work without it.

### Option 1: CLI installer (Recommended)

From the root of your project, run:

```bash
npx impeccable install
```

This shows the harness folders or installed CLIs it detected (for example `~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, `~/.grok`, `~/.hermes`, `~/.veto`, or project-local `.cursor`), lets you keep the detected set or customize providers, then asks whether to install into the current project or globally. Use `--providers=claude,codex,replit,cursor,grok,hermes,veto` and `--scope=project|global` to skip those choices in scripts. On Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, and Grok Build, it also installs the provider-native hook manifest for the current project. Veto receives the packaged skill under `~/.veto/skills/` and does not run native Impeccable edit hooks. Works with Cursor, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, Replit Agent, Grok Build, Hermes Agent, Veto, and every other supported tool. Reload your harness afterward.

To refresh an existing install, run:

```bash
npx impeccable update
```

Codex users should open `/hooks` after install or update and approve the project hook when prompted. Codex tracks trust by hook definition, so updates that change `.codex/hooks.json` can require approval again. Grok Build users need project folder trust (`/hooks-trust` or launch with `--trust`) before `.grok/hooks/` scripts run.

See [Allow the hook in your harness](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks#allow-the-hook-in-your-harness) for harness-specific trust and verification steps.

### Option 2: Git Submodule

For teams that want to keep Impeccable vendored and updated through Git, add this repo as a submodule and link the compiled provider build into your harness folders:

```bash
git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable .impeccable
npx impeccable link --source=.impeccable --providers=claude,cursor
git add .gitmodules .impeccable .claude .cursor
git commit -m "Add Impeccable skills"
```

Use the providers your project needs, for example `claude`, `cursor`, `gemini`, `codex`, `github`, `grok`, `devin`, `hermes`, `opencode`, `pi`, `qoder`, `trae`, `trae-cn`, `rovo-dev`, `vibe`, or `veto`. The command links individual skill folders from `.impeccable/dist/universal/` and leaves existing real skill directories untouched unless you pass `--force`.

To update later:

```bash
git submodule update --remote .impeccable
npx impeccable link --source=.impeccable --providers=claude,cursor
```

### Option 3: Plugin install

**GitHub Copilot in VS Code:**

Install [Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=renaissance-geek.impeccable), or run:

```bash
code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable
```

Requires VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat access, and a trusted local workspace. Open Chat in Agent mode and try `/impeccable polish`. This skill-only extension does not install automatic hooks; avoid a duplicate Impeccable skill in the same workspace/profile. See [VS Code distribution details](docs/VSCODE-EXTENSION.md).

**Claude Code:**
```bash
/plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable
```

> Claude Code only. After adding the marketplace, open `/plugin` and install Impeccable from the list.

**Grok Build:**
```bash
grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust
```

> Grok Build only. The `#plugin` suffix installs the slim plugin package (skills, agents, and hooks) instead of the full monorepo. Then run `/impeccable init` in a Grok session. Project-scoped installs via `npx impeccable install --providers=grok` also work and write `.grok/skills/` plus `.grok/hooks/impeccable.json`.

### Option 4: Download from Website

Visit [impeccable.style](https://impeccable.style), download the ZIP for your tool, and extract to your project.

### Option 5: Copy from Repository

**Cursor:**
```bash
cp -r dist/cursor/.cursor your-project/
```

> **Note:** Cursor skills require setup:
> 1. Switch to Nightly channel in Cursor Settings → Beta
> 2. Enable Agent Skills in Cursor Settings → Rules
>
> [Learn more about Cursor skills](https://cursor.com/docs/context/skills)

**Claude Code:**
```bash
# Project-specific
cp -r dist/claude-code/.claude your-project/

# Or global (applies to all projects)
cp -r dist/claude-code/.claude/* ~/.claude/
```

**OpenCode:**
```bash
cp -r dist/opencode/.opencode your-project/
```

**DeepSeek Harness:**
```bash
# Project-specific
cp -r dist/dsh/.dsh your-project/

# Or global (applies to all projects)
mkdir -p "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills"
cp -r dist/dsh/.dsh/skills/* "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/"
```

The CLI honors `DSH_HOME` only when it resolves inside your home directory (or to home itself); otherwise it uses `~/.dsh`. An outside-home manual copy is not managed by `impeccable install/update`.

**Devin:**
```bash
# Project-specific (Devin web, CLI, and Desktop all read .devin/skills/)
cp -r dist/devin/.devin your-project/

# Or global (Devin CLI and Desktop; use %APPDATA%\devin\skills on Windows)
mkdir -p "${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/devin/skills"
cp -r dist/devin/.devin/skills/* "${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/devin/skills/"
```

**Hermes Agent:**
```bash
# Global (applies to all projects; uses the active profile, or ~/.hermes by default)
cp -r dist/hermes/.hermes/skills/* "${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/"

# Or project-specific
cp -r dist/hermes/.hermes your-project/
```

> **Note:** Hermes gates project-local skills behind a per-repo trust decision
> (they are procedure documents, so auto-loading them from any cloned repo is
> treated as a prompt-injection vector). After a project-scoped install, run
> `hermes skills trust` once from the project root. Global installs into the
> active `$HERMES_HOME/skills/` (or `~/.hermes/skills/` when unset) load without
> a trust step. `/impeccable <command>` then
> routes through the skill's Commands table; the design hook does not install
> on Hermes (no hook surface).
>
> [Learn more about Hermes skills](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/skills)

**Pi:**
```bash
cp -r dist/pi/.pi your-project/
```

**Gemini CLI:**
```bash
cp -r dist/gemini/.gemini your-project/
```

> **Note:** Gemini CLI skills require setup:
> 1. Install preview version: `npm i -g @google/gemini-cli@preview`
> 2. Run `/settings` and enable "Skills"
> 3. Run `/skills list` to verify installation
>
> [Learn more about Gemini CLI skills](https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/skills/)

**Codex CLI:**
```bash
# Project-local
cp -r dist/agents/.agents your-project/
mkdir -p your-project/.codex
cp dist/codex/.codex/hooks.json your-project/.codex/hooks.json

# Or install the skill user-wide. Copy .codex/hooks.json into each project
# where you want the design hook to run.
mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills
cp -r dist/agents/.agents/skills/* ~/.agents/skills/
```

# ECC Your agent can write code, but ECC gives it a coordinated engineering system and toolbox: it plans before it builds, verifies changes with tests, reviews its own work from a fresh context, remembers what matters, and turns repeated wins into reusable skills and workflows. ```text plan -> test -> implement -> review -> verify -> remember -> improve ``` Instead of rebuilding that process in every prompt, you install it once and make it part of how your agent works. > Optimize the context window. Persist everything else. ECC is MIT-licensed open source. It works best with Claude Code today, has native Codex and Qoder plugin paths, and provides capability-limited adapters for Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini, Zed, GitHub Copilot, Antigravity, Qwen, and other harnesses. See the [support status matrix](#platform-support) before assuming feature parity. Access to 71 agents, 311 skills, and 97 legacy command shims, plus hooks, rules, memory, continuous learning, and AgentShield security scanning. --- ## 3.0 案例 下面这些都是 3.0 跑出来的。前五个是从发布时新跑的 6 道题里挑的，每道只给一句话需求，方向是 agent 自己挑的，作者没插手；后两个一个是第三轮盲选赢下来的那版，一个是发布后作者拿它做的真实项目。 ### 网页 · 《富岳三十六景》线上展 > 「给葛饰北斋的《富岳三十六景》做一个线上展览网站」 三版分别是 Rijksmuseum 官网式的暗场展厅、田中一光式的三角窗、民国书衣式的题签框。设计体检报过一次撞车：两版首屏都用了《神奈川冲浪里》，它就把暗场那版换成了《山下白雨》。

往下一章讲普鲁士蓝，依据是大都会博物馆的光谱研究；全 46 幅都来自芝加哥艺术博物馆和大都会的开放馆藏。

### App · 鸣迹（观鸟记录） > 「做一个观鸟记录 App 的原型」 现实参照找的是拿了 2025 年苹果设计奖的 CapWords，`ref_board.py` 先把它截成参考板，agent 亲眼看过再动手。借来的是「从照片里撕下一张贴纸」：每只鸟都从 Wikimedia 的真实照片里分割出来，贴进一年的本子里，叫声波形是拿真实录音算的。

### App · 今晚吃啥（家常菜谱） > 「做一个家常菜谱 App」 秒数轮盘恰好抽到吕敬人书籍设计，最后做成了一本菜谱：一道菜一页方子，切口旁边留一条旁注栏，写「擦干再煎才不溅油」「老抽只要几滴」，朱砂只给「开做」这一方印。外观账本看到最近 6 个交付里 5 个是无衬线标题，这一版挑了宋体。

### PPT · 《千里江山图》讲座 走的是最佳设计师 Abbott Miller 式的暗场展柜，暗底取的是绢地最暗处的颜色。封面底下那条细长的位置条就是整卷缩略图，框出这一页在 11.9 米长卷的哪一段。

### PPT · 黑洞的照片是怎么拍出来的 现实参照是 Jonathan Corum 的讲座幻灯片：黑底、照片做主角、标注直接写在图上。每页都标了出处，事实先过核查再上页面。

### App · 绿拇指（第三轮盲选赢的那版） 把植物当成会呼吸的生命体征来读。App 原型做成一张有构图的展示板，几台手机错落排开。

### 网页 · 旅居档案（作者自己的项目） 三年里所有旅行照片的地图。选的是葛西薰式的白纸明朝体长卷，开头一张卫星地图串起所有旅程，往下一段旅程一章。选完作者顺口说了句「尽量不要遗漏」，它就记进了经验：个人回忆类档案照片要全，而且注明只适用于照片档案，不外溢到产品界面。

--- ## 📺 新手教程（花叔亲录） 不知道怎么用？看花叔录的 huashu-design 上手教程：

👉 在 YouTube 观看完整教程

--- ## 装上就能用 ```bash npx skills add alchaincyf/huashu-design ``` > **装完先自检**：这个 skill 不只是 SKILL.md 一个文件，`references/`、`assets/`、`scripts/`、`demos/` 四个子目录里有 99 处被引用的配方、脚本、素材，缺一不可。装完看一眼安装目录（如 `~/.claude/skills/huashu-design/`），如果只有 SKILL.md、没有那几个子目录，说明你的 `skills` CLI 版本太旧（≤1.5.15 有个只同步单文件的 bug，已在 1.5.19 修复）。升级后再装一次即可： > > ```bash > npm i -g skills@latest # 或 npx skills@latest add alchaincyf/huashu-design > ``` > > 升级后仍异常，就用 `git clone` 兜底安装，把仓库克隆到任意 skills 目录即可： > > ```bash > git clone https://github.com/alchaincyf/huashu-design.git ~/.claude/skills/huashu-design > ``` 然后在 Claude Code / Codex / Cursor 等任意支持 skills 的 agent 里直接说话： ``` 「做一份 AI 心理学的演讲 PPT，推荐 3 个风格方向让我选」 「做个 AI 番茄钟 iOS 原型，4 个核心屏幕要真能点击」 「把这段逻辑做成 60 秒动画，导出 MP4 和 GIF」 「帮我对这个设计做一个 5 维度评审」 ``` 没有按钮、没有面板、没有 Figma 插件。 --- ## Star 趋势

--- ## 能做什么 | 能力 | 交付物 | 典型耗时 | |------|--------|----------| | 交互原型（App / Web） | 单文件 HTML · 真 iPhone bezel · 可点击 · Playwright 验证 | 10–15 min | | 演讲幻灯片 | HTML deck（浏览器演讲）+ 可编辑 PPTX（文本框保留） | 15–25 min | | 时间轴动画 | MP4（25fps / 60fps 插帧）+ GIF（palette 优化）+ BGM | 8–12 min | | 设计变体 | 3+ 并排对比 · Tweaks 实时调参 · 跨维度探索 | 10 min | | 信息图 / 可视化 | 印刷级排版 · 可导 PDF/PNG/SVG | 10 min | | 设计方向顾问 | **三套逻辑各出两个候选**（最佳设计师 + 同媒介获奖作品 + 秒数轮盘）· 六张缩略图挑三版真实视觉，另三张作备选 | 10 min | | 5 维度专家评审 | 雷达图 + Keep/Fix/Quick Wins · 可操作修复清单 | 3 min | --- ## Demo 画廊 ### 设计方向顾问 模糊需求时的 fallback：**三套互补逻辑各出两个候选**——最佳设计师（预算无上限时最适合的设计师）+ 现实参照（同媒介的获奖作品，先截图亲眼看）+ 秒数轮盘（从风格库随机抽，打破惯性）。六个候选先画成一页缩略图，挑最强、最不一样的三版做成**真实视觉**让你看着选，另外三张作为备选一起给你。背后是 **84 种 HTML 原生风格库**（网页 20 + PPT 20 + 信息图 20 + App 12 + 中文与东亚 12，纯 CSS 无需生图），每种都有一张样张。

动图为 2.0 流程（三套逻辑直接各出一版）

3.0 新增的两个分区，每格都是一张样张（全部纯 HTML/CSS，题材与数字虚构）：

### iOS App 原型 iPhone 15 Pro 精确机身（灵动岛 / 状态栏 / Home Indicator）· 状态驱动多屏切换 · 真图从 Wikimedia/Met/Unsplash 取 · Playwright 自动点击测试。

### Motion Design 引擎 Stage + Sprite 时间片段模型 · `useTime` / `useSprite` / `interpolate` / `Easing` 四 API 覆盖所有动画需求 · 一条命令导出 MP4 / GIF / 60fps 插帧 / 带 BGM 的成片。

### HTML Slides → 可编辑 PPTX HTML deck 浏览器演讲 · `html2pptx.js` 读 DOM 的 computedStyle 逐元素翻译成 PowerPoint 对象 · 导出的是**真文本框**，PPT 里双击即可编辑。

### Tweaks · 实时变体切换 配色 / 字型 / 信息密度等参数化 · 侧边面板切换 · 纯前端 + `localStorage` 持久化 · 刷新不丢。

### 信息图 / 数据可视化 杂志级排版 · CSS Grid 精准分栏 · `text-wrap: pretty` 排印细节 · 真数据驱动 · 可导 PDF 矢量 / PNG 300dpi / SVG。

### 5 维度专家评审 哲学一致性 · 视觉层级 · 细节执行 · 功能性 · 创新性 各 0–10 分 · 雷达图可视化 · 输出 Keep / Fix / Quick Wins 清单。

### Junior Designer 工作流 不闷头做大招：先写 assumptions + placeholders + reasoning，尽早 show 给你，再迭代。理解错了早改比晚改便宜 100 倍。

### 品牌资产协议 5 步硬流程 涉及具体品牌时强制执行：问 → 搜 → 下载（三条兜底）→ grep 色值 → 写 `brand-spec.md`。

--- ## Showcase · 2.0 时期的真实案例 ### 鹦鹉进化史网站 · 设计方向顾问三套逻辑实战（2.0） > **Live demo · [https://www.huasheng.ai/parrots/](https://www.huasheng.ai/parrots/)** 一句「做个介绍鹦鹉进化史的网站」、零额外要求，skill 自动跑完整 2.0 顾问流程：先判断图片是内容必需 → 抓公共领域博物插画（Edward Lear / John Gould 的鹦鹉图录）→ **三套逻辑并行**（秒数轮盘 + 现实参照获奖站 + 原研哉「白」哲学）各出一版真实视觉。**素材齐了再设计，不是边设计边用色块占位。** ### 「聊聊 skill」 · PM after-party 演讲 deck > **Live demo · [https://skill-huasheng.vercel.app](https://skill-huasheng.vercel.app)** 13 页 HTML deck，**全部用 huashu-design 完成**： - 黑底极简衬线视觉系统（cover / about / hook / what / why / closing） - 2 个带 BGM + SFX 的 22 秒 cinematic demo（Nuwa skill workflow + Darwin skill workflow），各采用**完全独立的视觉语言**： - **Nuwa**：3D 知识 orbit + Pentagon 提炼 + SKILL.md typewriter + 「21 分钟」hero reveal - **Darwin**：autoresearch loop spin + v1/v5 并列 diff + Hill-Climb 全屏曲线 + Ratchet gear lock - 每个 cinematic 默认显示**完整静态 workflow dashboard**（观众随时能看清 skill 怎么跑），点 ▶ 才触发动画，跑完自动 fade 回 dashboard - 嵌入 huasheng.ai 的 25 秒 hero 动画（iframe 本地化兜底） - 真实数据：14,495 stargazers 真实曲线（gh API 拉取）+ DeepSeek V4 真实 specs（WebSearch 验证） - 真实 AI 素材：用 `huashu-gpt-image` 跑 4×2 grid 大图，`extract_grid.py` 抠出 8 张独立透明 PNG，做 3D orbit 漂浮 **适合参考的页面**： - `/slides/slide-04b-nuwa-flow.html` · 静态 dashboard + cinematic overlay 双层架构 - `/slides/slide-06b-darwin-flow.html` · 完全独立视觉语言的对照案例 - `/slides/slide-03b-deepseek-cover.html` · AI slop vs 真实设计师视角的对比页 详细 cinematic patterns 见 `references/cinematic-patterns.md`。 --- ## 核心机制 ### 品牌资产协议 skill 里最硬的一段规则。涉及具体品牌（Stripe、Linear、Anthropic、自家公司等）时强制执行 5 步： | 步骤 | 动作 | 目的 | |------|------|------| | 1 · 问 | 用户有 brand guidelines 吗？ | 尊重已有资源 | | 2 · 搜官方品牌页 | `.com/brand` · `brand..com` · `.com/press` | 抓权威色值 | | 3 · 下载资产 | SVG 文件 → 官网 HTML 全文 → 产品截图取色 | 三条兜底，前一条失败立刻走下一条 | | 4 · grep 提取色值 | 从资产里抓所有 `#xxxxxx`，按频率排序，过滤黑白灰 | **绝不从记忆猜品牌色** | | 5 · 固化 spec | 写 `brand-spec.md` + CSS 变量，所有 HTML 引用 `var(--brand-*)` | 不固化就会忘 | A/B 测试（v1 vs v2，各跑 6 agent）：**v2 的稳定性方差比 v1 低 5 倍**。稳定性的稳定性，这是 skill 真正的护城河。 ### 设计方向顾问（Fallback） 当用户需求模糊到无法着手时触发（3.0 重做）： - 先对话澄清 + 主动索要参考（名字 / logo / 品牌色 / 喜欢的参考站），只问一轮 - 取齐内容必需的真图（公共领域 / 免版权，脚本一键抓），再开工 - **三套逻辑各出两个候选，共六个**：① 最佳设计师（两位气质不同的设计师，用他们的思维从头做）② 现实参照（两件**同媒介**的获奖作品——做 App 找 App、做 deck 找出版物；`scripts/ref_board.py` 先截图亲眼看，再拆网格、字号比和色彩比例）③ 秒数轮盘（`date +%S` 取秒，在产出形态对应的分区和中文东亚分区各抽一号，先看样张再动手） - **六张缩略图 → 挑三版做完整稿**：单看够好、彼此不一样、不撞你最近的项目；没选上的三张作为备选一起给你，看中哪张再做 - **绝不让你在没看到视觉时盲选风格**——摆出来就停，看着选 - 底层是 **84 种 HTML 原生风格库**，每种配一张样张和源码（`assets/style-specimens/`），作弹药，不是教条 为什么这样做：我们拿固定题目做了三轮改前改后盲选（内部测试）。第一轮强制每版套一个大隐喻，页面被做成道具，4 题只赢 1 题；第二轮为了躲 AI 默认外观加了一堆禁令，三版一起变得「太规整，太无聊」，2 题全输；第三轮改成加选项、不加禁令——多出候选、给看得见的样张、看真参考——同两道题都赢了。 ### 越用越懂你：经验、外观账本与设计体检 - **经验**：`scripts/learn.py` 开工前带出你说过的品味原话（「太素了」「A 的结构加 C 的颜色」）和过去的教训，收工时把值得记的记下来；记录前会告诉你，不想记可以拒绝 - **外观账本**：每次交付记一

repository.description: Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents.

details.readme:
Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents.

Studio | Quickstart | Showcase | Playground | Catalog | Docs | Discord

HyperFrames is an open-source framework for turning HTML, CSS, media, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. Use it locally with the CLI, from AI coding agents with skills, or as the rendering core behind hosted authoring workflows. Using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or another coding agent? Run `npx hyperframes skills update` once, then ask your agent to make a video. ## Quick Start ### With an AI coding agent For Claude Code, install the versioned plugin: ```bash claude plugin marketplace add heygen-com/hyperframes claude plugin install hyperframes@hyperframes ``` To enable auto-update for the **hyperframes** marketplace, run `claude` in a terminal in your project. In Claude Code's terminal UI, run `/plugin`, then select **Marketplaces** → **hyperframes** → **Enable auto-update**. Afterward, use `/hyperframes:hyperframes`. See the [plugin guide](docs/guides/plugins.mdx) for Copilot, VS Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, updates, and migration. For standalone skills (including OpenCode), use: ```bash npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes ``` > The picker opens with nothing pre-selected — the **Core Skills** group is all you need; `/slideshow`, `/remotion-to-hyperframes` and `/figma` install on demand. Agents and non-interactive runs should use `npx hyperframes skills update` instead — it installs exactly the core set, whereas `skills add --all` installs all 7 published skills. The six repo-internal skills under `.claude/skills` / `.agents/skills` are excluded by default. For the full published set use `npx hyperframes skills`. > > `skills add` resolves the skills.sh registry blob, which can lag `main` by hours. `npx hyperframes skills update` installs from the current `main`, so reach for it when you need the newest copy of a skill. Run project-local installs from your video project's directory. From a HyperFrames checkout, use `npx hyperframes skills update` for a global install instead: a project-local installer target can overlap the tracked `skills/` source and overwrite uncommitted edits. See [contributor setup](CONTRIBUTING.md#getting-started). Try a prompt like: > Using `/hyperframes`, create a 10-second product intro with a fade-in title, a background video, and subtle background music. The skills teach agents the HyperFrames production loop: plan the video, write valid HTML, wire seekable animations, add media, lint, preview, and render. They work with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, IBM Bob, and other coding agents that support skills. ## Skills HyperFrames ships 7 skills. Make any video by asking for it; the `/hyperframes` skill carries the contract and the references (film, captions, overlays, motion, look). Read it first. For standalone installation, default to the **core set** (`/hyperframes`, `/hyperframes-cli`, `/hyperframes-registry`, `/media-use`). `npx hyperframes skills update` installs exactly that from anywhere; the interactive picker (`npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes`) lists it as the "Core Skills" group, nothing pre-selected. The picker is interactive-only — a non-interactive or agent run without `--skill` installs all 7. Use `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --all` to install the complete published set deliberately (skips the picker), or `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --skill ` for just one (bare name, no leading `/`). Standalone installs stay lean after that: `npx hyperframes init` installs the **core set** only when it is missing and never touches a skill you already have (`npx hyperframes skills update` refreshes them, and never removes one); `/figma`, `/slideshow` and `/remotion-to-hyperframes` install **on demand** with `npx hyperframes skills update `. Nothing re-pulls the full set behind your back. ### Plugin packages Plugins bundle the full skill catalog and use their agent's update manager. `bun run package:agent-plugin` builds the committed portable ZIP, source metadata, and SHA-256 checksum. See the [maintainer checklist](docs/contributing/agent-plugins.mdx). ### Upload to Codex Build the upload-ready Codex plugin archive from the committed `HEAD` version of the manifest, brand assets, and skills: ```bash bun run package:codex-plugin ``` This writes `dist/hyperframes-plugin.zip` with a `hyperframes/` root folder and fails if the archive exceeds Codex's 100 MB upload limit. ### Core set | Skill | Use when | | ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `/hyperframes` | **Read first** for any request to make, edit, animate or render a video, motion graphic, captions or overlays with HyperFrames (HTML rendered to video). Holds the render contract and the work loop, and points to the references for format, motion, look, captions, whole films and storyboards. | | `/hyperframes-cli` | The HyperFrames CLI by job — scaffold, check, look at frames, edit the timeline, preview, render locally or in the cloud, publish, project history — plus reading its JSON and recovering from build or render failures. | | `/hyperframes-registry` | About 450 ready-made blocks and components installed as editable source — transitions, overlays, titles, kinetic type, captions, charts, maps, 3D, camera moves. Use before hand-building any named visual; also for `hyperframes add` and `catalog`. | | `/media-use` | Get or make any media for a video — music, sound effects, images, icons, logos, voiceover, avatar and generated video, transcripts, cutouts, colour grades and looks — with HeyGen or free local tools, and mix placed audio. Also for footage that looks dark, flat or dull. | ### On demand | Skill | Use when | | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `/figma` | Bring Figma into a video — rendered assets, brand tokens, components, storyboard frames as reconstructed motion, shaders and connector-assisted motion. Use when you paste a figma.com link. | | `/slideshow` | A presentation, pitch deck or interactive deck — discrete slides, fragment reveals, branching, hotspot navigation, presenter mode with speaker notes. Output is a navigable deck, not a rendered MP4. | | `/remotion-to-hyperframes` | Bringing existing video code or footage into HyperFrames (Remotion first; also Motion Canvas, Lottie, Three.js, canvas, other tools' renders), verified frame by frame. | For visual design handoff workflows, see the [Claude Design guide](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/claude-design) and [Open Design guide](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/open-design). ### Manually with the CLI ```bash npx hyperframes init my-video cd my-video npx hyperframes preview # preview in browser with live reload npx hyperframes render # render to MP4 ``` **Requirements:** Node.js 22+, FFmpeg ## What You Can Build Need ideas? Browse the [Showcase](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/showcase) for finished videos you can watch, read, run, and remix. - Product launch videos and feature announcements - PR walkthroughs with animated code diffs, narration, and captions - Data visualizations, chart races, and map animations - Social videos with kinetic captions, overlays, and music - Docs-to-video, PDF-to-video, and site-tour explainers - Reusable motion graphics for automated content pipelines ## Frame.md **frame.md — your design system, ready for video.** Every brand has a `design.md`. None of them were written for a camera. `frame.md` is the missing translation layer: it takes your web-context design spec and inverts it for the frame — the same tokens, the same rules, but rewritten so an AI agent can compose a promo video without guessing at scale or reaching for web chrome. The output is a `DESIGN.md` superset your whole toolchain can read. Atoms stay sacred. Composition stays free. Numbers come from the script.

repository.description: Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3 rewritten from scratch in Rust, checked against vanilla with 281 differential harnesses. Get it with the Horizon launcher.

details.readme:
Website · Download · Documentation · Release notes · Roadmap · Project status · Contributing

# Horizon Horizon is Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3 rewritten in Rust: a native game that reads the same worlds, follows the same rules and generates the same terrain as the Java game, and is checked against it by 281 differential harnesses. You play it through a small launcher, on the files from your own copy of Minecraft. It is free, open source and unofficial. > Not an official Minecraft product. Not approved by or associated with Mojang or Microsoft. Horizon contains no Minecraft code, assets or data: you need your own legally obtained copy of Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3. ## Download Horizon is installed through **the Horizon launcher**. Get it from [playhorizon.dev](https://playhorizon.dev) (the Download button picks your system) or from [the launcher releases](https://github.com/ludovic111/horizon/releases?q=launcher-v&expanded=true), for Linux x86-64, macOS on Apple Silicon or Windows x64. The launcher installs and updates the game, prepares its files from your own copy of Minecraft, and updates itself. **You need** Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3, played once (the official launcher, Prism, MultiMC and other launchers all work); a Java 25 runtime, for the one-time preparation; and a GPU with Vulkan on Linux and Windows, or any Apple Silicon Mac. Step by step, with macOS's first-open prompt and the first launch: [Install and first launch](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/install).
## What works today The [documentation](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/) covers each of these. - **The game:** singleplayer with vanilla's world generation, mobs, villagers, raids, redstone, every command, the HUD and the recipe book, on saves in vanilla's format. Worlds from 1.8 to 26.2 are upgraded as vanilla does. [Status table](#project-status). - **Horizon's own extras:** new menus (vanilla's are one setting away), graphics presets, distant terrain up to 1024 chunks, controller support, optional zoom, minimap and more, all off by default where they would change the vanilla look. See [Settings](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/settings). - **Resource packs and data packs:** resource packs work, and data packs load functions, predicates and item modifiers. - **Playing with others:** invite friends from the pause menu's Friends button with a code, Open to LAN, and joining offline-mode servers. Horizon cannot sign in to a Microsoft account yet, so it cannot join servers that check accounts. See [Multiplayer](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/multiplayer). - **Mods:** Horizon has its own mod system (Rust compiled to WebAssembly). Java mod jars do not run. See [Mods and data packs](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/mods). Screenshots, captured in the Rust client itself with vanilla assets and no mods or shaders:
## Host a server The launcher's **Servers** page creates, starts, backs up and updates a Horizon server with buttons, and invites friends over Tailscale. On a VPS, `horizon-server` installs with one command and runs without Java. Guide: [Host a server](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/hosting) ([reference](docs/hosting.md)). ## Modpacks The launcher's **Modpacks** page imports a Modrinth or CurseForge pack, shows which of its mods Horizon can carry over, and plays the ones it can as their own profile. Today that means content mods made of data and assets; mods with Java code are not ported yet. See [Modpacks](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/modpacks). ## Agent control AI agents and scripts can play Horizon. `horizon-ctl`, shipped beside the game in every release folder, is a command line that reads the game as JSON and acts like a player; `horizon-ctl mcp` serves the same commands as an MCP server (one tool per command, screenshots returned as images). ```sh horizon-ctl launch --world Survival --seed 5 --wait # finds the version the launcher installed horizon-ctl state # position, health, food, target, screen... horizon-ctl find-block birch_log # the nearest logs horizon-ctl goto -0.5 65 -2.5 --near 2.5 # walks there along a path horizon-ctl break -1 65 -3 # mines it; replies with the drops horizon-ctl open-inventory && horizon-ctl click-slot 0 # menus: slots, buttons by label, text fields ``` Commands block until the action is done and reply with what happened; errors are JSON with distinct exit codes, `horizon-ctl help` lists every command and `horizon-ctl COMMAND --help` explains one with examples. It talks to the game over a Unix socket on Linux and macOS and over a token-protected localhost port on Windows. See [Agent control in the native client guide](docs/native-client.md#agent-control-horizon-ctl-and-mcp). ## Build from source For developers. Requirements: Rust 1.90 or newer, Python 3.10 or newer, JDK 25, and on Linux the ALSA and udev development headers (`libasound2-dev libudev-dev` on Debian and Ubuntu). Development and the vanilla harnesses run on Linux. Horizon contains no game files and never downloads them. It builds its resources from **your own copy** of Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3, verified against the checksums in `research-lock.json`: 1. **Client:** install Java Edition with the official launcher and play 26.3 once. Horizon reads `versions/26.3/`, `libraries/` and `assets/` from the launcher's game directory (`~/.minecraft` on Linux). If yours lives elsewhere, pass `--minecraft-dir` or set `HORIZON_MINECRAFT_DIR`. 2. **Server jar:** the 26.3 server jar, from the `downloads.server.url` in your launcher's `versions/26.3/26.3.json` (or [minecraft.net/download/server](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/download/server) while 26.3 is the current release). Pass it with `--server-jar` or set `HORIZON_SERVER_JAR`. It is only needed the first time. ```sh git clone https://github.com/ludovic111/horizon.git cd horizon cargo run --release -p horizon-prepare -- --prepare --server-jar ~/Downloads/server.jar # needs JDK 25 cargo run --release -p horizon-prepare -- sounds # optional: sounds from your launcher install cargo run --release -p horizon-client ``` Everything prepared lands in the gitignored `.local/`. It is derived from the game: never commit it or share it. The client starts on the title screen. Command-line options (`--world`, `--seed`, `--creative`, `--render-distance`, `--dedicated`), controls, scripting through `horizon-ctl` and the architecture are described in [the native client guide](docs/native-client.md). The rest of the developer documentation is indexed in [docs/README.md](docs/README.md), including [the parity workflow](docs/parity-workflow.md). ## Roadmap What is being done now, what comes next and where you can help, in plain words and in technical detail: [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md). [playhorizon.dev/hub](https://playhorizon.dev/hub) shows it with the work board, the journal of what shipped and how to help. ## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome: see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for how we work (vanilla first, small pull requests, labels), or [the contributing guide](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/contributing) on the site. Questions and ideas: [Discord](https://discord.gg/HcTeMZxe5E). Before opening a pull request, run the self-check and paste the block it prints: ```sh git config core.hooksPath .githooks python3 tools/pr_ready.py ``` It runs rustfmt, clippy with warnings denied, the tests of the crates you touched, the Python tests, the public-tree check, and the vanilla harnesses your change can affect. CI runs the same checks on GitHub's Linux runners; the vanilla harnesses need the game, which Horizon never downloads, so they run on a maintainer's computer holding their own copy. Never commit game files, decompiled source or prepared resources: `tools/check_public_tree.py` rejects them, and tracked Java is allowed only under the project's own `dev/horizonlab` namespace. ## Project status The table below is the project's own audit of each subsystem. Every subsystem now matches vanilla in every harness that compares it. 100% means 100% of what the harnesses compare, not proof that nothing else differs. The remaining known differences are listed below. ### Java parity: 100% Each subsystem scores 0 (absent), 0.25 (started, not playable), 0.5 (playable, major vanilla features missing), 0.75 (playable, mostly complete) or 1 (complete and verified against vanilla by differential tests). The percentage is the average; `tests/test_parity.py` keeps it in sync with this table. Last audited 2026-10-13 against the harness results: all 281 harnesses pass on Linux, each rerun whenever one of its inputs changed, and the Mac mini now runs every one of them too (Rust uses Java's own float maths on each platform). | Subsystem | Score | Main gaps | | --- | ---: | --- | | Window, input and game loop | 1 | None: the game loop, options, camera, auto-jump, toggle sprint/sneak, local input and the frame limiter match vanilla | | Assets and resources | 1 | None: item models match vanilla over 196,290 stacks and the client draws every item through them; the resource pack screen matches vanilla's drawing over 3,000 sessions of clicks, scrolling and searching, its incompatibility confirmation included | | Network protocol and multiplayer | 1 | None: joins vanilla servers; the dedicated server (`--dedicated`) matches vanilla's files, status ping, login, configuration, play, chunks, chat, recipes, advancements and command tree, a client built from vanilla's packet code joins it, Horizon joins a vanilla server, and LAN disco
